newsitem.title: GERMANY: German forex, money mkt groups considering merger.
newsitem.headline: German forex, money mkt groups considering merger.

text.p: Germany's foreign exchange traders' association and money market traders' association are considering a merger in the run-up to European monetary union, the money traders group (VdG) said on Tuesday.
The VdG said the boards of the two associations had agreed almost unanimously to negotiate on terms for a merger.
The working title for the new group is Finanzmarktverband Deutschland (the German financial market association).
"We are hoping to put this into effect by spring 1998 at the latest," VdG board member Burkhard Skibbe.
The VdG said the decision to plan a merger with the forex group was taken because there would no longer be a clear division of labour between the two groups in a single currency environment.

"When the euro comes there will be no mark money market trasurers and no mark spot traders," the VdG said. That meant there would be no further need for mark money market trading, but rather trade in whichever currencies were available at the time, it added.

The activities of money and exchange rate traders would thus no longer be clearly divided, it said. In other major European centres such as London and Paris, money and foreign exchange dealers already jointly expressed their interests to central banks, governments and other financial centres.
The VdG represents 735 money market traders, while Forex Deutschland has around 1,350 members.
The VdG said it was not yet certain that it would achieve the 75 percent majority needed to approve a merger.
The association said that a considerable number of regulatory decisions had to be taken in advance of the start of EMU in 1999.
As one example, the association said that so far a single reference interest rate for banks in the euro zone, nicknamed "euribor" in the parlance of the money market traders.
"It cannot be allowed to be the case that as is the case today for the mark, the London LIBOR provides the benchmark for the euro money market," the VdG said.

The association recommended that each country taking part in EMU should calculate its own Euribor on the basis of the usual national practices and that these be used to calculate an non-weighted average rate for the EMU are as a whole.
